issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires implementing a private helper function internal_calc ("nicht global"). The reference solution, however, exports internal_calc by declaring it global (line 'global internal_calc') in solution_repository/helloWorld.asm. This contradicts the specification and may confuse students about whether internal_calc should be a private/local symbol or an exported/global one.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution match the specification by removing the 'global internal_calc' directive from solution_repository/helloWorld.asm so internal_calc remains a private/local symbol. Alternatively, if exporting the function was intentional, update the problem statement to allow/internal_calc to be global and explain why.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires implementing `internal_calc` as a private helper ("nicht global"), but the solution repository exports `internal_calc` as a global symbol (`global internal_calc`) and defines it at top-level. This mismatch between the expected visibility (private) and the solution's exported/global declaration can confuse students about the intended scope/visibility of `internal_calc` and whether they should declare it global or keep it private.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the artifacts consistent: either (A) update the solution to keep `internal_calc` private (remove the `global internal_calc` export so it is not exported), or (B) if exporting is intended, update the problem statement to allow/mention a globally exported `internal_calc`. Preferred fix: remove `global internal_calc` from solution_repository/helloWorld.asm so the implementation matches the problem instruction that `internal_calc` be a private helper.
